- [LEXP.7.3a] **`**` with an integer exponent is an exception to [LEXP.7.2].**
  `Int ** Int` is `Int` **only** when the exponent is a compile-time-known
  **non-negative** integer (a literal, or a `const` that folds to ≥ 0); the
  result is `xʸ` computed by **binary exponentiation**, which agrees bit-for-bit
  with linear repeated multiplication because `ds_i64_mul`'s wrap contract makes
  integer multiplication associative modulo 2⁶⁴ — the grouping is therefore not
  observable and the spec does not have to pick one. When the exponent is a
  **negative** integer, or an `Int` whose sign is not known at compile time, the
  result is **`Float`**, computed by the **correctly-rounded `pow`**
  ([LEXP.3.9.2]) — so `2 ** -3 == 0.125` ([LEXP.1.3]), and `0 ** negative` is
  `+Inf`, `±Inf` for an odd exponent ([LEXP.3.9.3]). A non-integer exponent, or
  a `Float` operand, gives `Float` by the same `pow`. Correct rounding
  determines that result **uniquely**, and that is what makes every form EXACT
  and cross-platform bit-identical ([LDET.3.3a.4]) rather than merely
  reproducible. This keeps the static type sound: an integer power that can go
  fractional is typed `Float`, never silently `Int`.
